cohort: The study included 222 women with asymptomatic obstetric anal sphincter lesions diagnosed by ultrasound during their second pregnancy.
finding: Planned cesarean section for the second delivery did not significantly reduce the risk of anal incontinence at 6 months postpartum compared to planned vaginal delivery in women with asymptomatic obstetric anal sphincter lesions.
gest_age: Third trimester of the second pregnancy
